candidates.title: bounded-chainer-drain-and-lower-only-detection-followon
candidates.description: Reopen ADR-016's NO-GO on the bounded cross-member ChainerBackend drain AND close the lower-only survivor blind spot (both reopen TOGETHER per ADR-016 M2) IF R4 is falsified: a reachable >=2-distinct-secure-store chain appears (macOS multi-keychain / Linux multi-collection = two instances of the SAME allowlisted-secure class at DISTINCT stores), OR a future keyring exposes a portable per-member delete / a fan-out delete. Implement a bounded single-pass drain over the enumerable .backends (terminates by construction) + read-back lower members.
candidates.rationale: ADR-016 recorded NO-GO grounded on R4 (near-unreachability) + Parnas information-hiding/YAGNI, reversibility cheap. This is the pre-registered reopen trigger so the deferral is traceable, not silent. slice-008 AC1 confirmed the real chainer does NOT fan-out its delete, so today the drain has ~zero real callers.

candidates.title: harden-cred-lifecycle-ci-runner-pinning-and-dedup
candidates.description: Harden .github/workflows/cred-lifecycle-real.yml: (1) pin runs-on: ubuntu-latest to a currently-GA image (ubuntu-24.04) for reproducibility parity with the macos-15 pin M1 already applied; (2) suppress the duplicate co-resident run -- a first push to the default branch auto-fires an on:push:paths run co-resident with workflow_dispatch (empirically confirmed at slice-010: push run 29228636585 + dispatch run 29228832579 both ran the macOS leg = double macOS billing). Add a concurrency: group (cancel-in-progress) keyed on the workflow+ref, and/or scope on:push:branches, so only one run per ref survives.
candidates.rationale: slice-010 pinned only macOS (M1); ubuntu-latest stays on a moving label (expert-lens deferred). And the push/dispatch duplication doubles 10x-billed macOS minutes on every real-runner proof. Both are cheap in-scope CI-harness edits that make the next backend-adapter CI proof (Ollama/Codex/Antigravity) reproducible + cheaper.

assumptions.statement: A concurrency group with cancel-in-progress cancels the co-resident push run without cancelling the intended dispatch (order-independent), and ubuntu-24.04 carries the same gnome-keyring/setcap incantations as ubuntu-latest did.
assumptions.fallback: If concurrency cancels the wrong run, scope on:push:branches to exclude the integration branch instead.

candidates.verification_plan: Dispatch once on a fresh push; confirm exactly ONE run per ref survives (the dispatch), both legs green on the pinned images, AC-style executed-count assertion still HARD-REDs a vacuous run.

candidates.title: wire-rebase-freshness-guard-into-ci-advisory-or-git-hook
candidates.description: The out_of_scope follow-on from slice-011: optionally wire tools/rebase_freshness_check.py into the aivlc repo's OWN infra -- an advisory CI job and/or a local git pre-* hook -- so the freshness warning fires automatically before /validate-slice, WITHOUT touching the READ-ONLY aisdlc-v2 pipeline (forbidden by CLAUDE.md). MUST handle shallow clones (critique m2): a CI --depth=1 checkout truncates history and would flip a genuinely-stale branch to a silent UNKNOWN (fail-open no-warn, never a false STALE) -- run on a full clone or `git fetch --unshallow` first. Small polish to fold in from /code-review: CR1 -- ADR-017's 'even a bug cannot emit non-zero' is overstated because argparse.parse_args() exits 2 on a typo'd flag BEFORE main()'s catch-all (wrap parse_args, or narrow the ADR wording); CR2 -- add a direct test for the defensive rc>1/rc128 ancestry branch (currently unreachable with a verified ref, untested).
candidates.rationale: mission-brief out_of_scope explicitly names 'optional git-hook / CI-advisory wiring inside the aivlc repo's own infra (possible follow-on, not this cut)'. The guard SHIPPED as a manual dev tool (slice-011) but nothing auto-invokes it yet; auto-wiring makes the stale-base discovery automatic rather than opt-in. Low urgency -- the manual tool already retires the R-14 process risk; this is convenience + the two advisory code-review minors.
